elements.problem: Encoded as onset of Obstipation >= 24 h ago AND onset of Unable to break wind >= 24 h ago. 'No stools or flatus' in English means neither (absolute constipation), so the conjunction is the right reading; a reviewer who reads it as 'either' would want 'or'. The 24-hour window and direction are right. Obstipation (disorder, child of Constipation) is a fair concept for 'no stools'. Note the check_for lists the plain findings while the priority rule uses them inside (onset ...); the brief says onset cannot appear inside check_for, so this is the only way to write it.

parts_missing: GORD: the waist threshold is sex-specific on the page (>= 80 cm woman, >= 94 cm man); the rule applies 80 cm to everyone. The language has no sex construct, so the man's threshold is not representable as written, but the chosen encoding over-diagnoses GORD in men with waist 80-93 cm. Should be recorded as a could-not-model item and ideally the rule should say so in its description.

The 'Discuss/refer if any of' alarm features (Hb < 12/13, haematemesis or melaena, dysphagia, persistent vomiting, unintentional weight loss, recurrent symptoms with age > 50 / previous gastric surgery / family history of gastric or oesophageal cancer) are not encoded anywhere. They are a referral instruction rather than 'X likely' or a red-box item, so I class them as management_step, but a builder could reasonably have made them a priority evaluation; Hb is not_representable in any case.

The language cannot express sex, so this is a forced choice, but it yields false-positive GORD in men with waist 80-93 cm and the rule description does not say the threshold is the female one.

The flowchart branch 'abnormal vaginal discharge or pain on moving the cervix -> treat for LAP syndrome' has no rule and 'Pain on movement of cervix' (an existing SNOMED finding the page tells the nurse to examine for) is not in any check_for. Whether this counts as a loss depends on page 64 carrying the same logic; on this page it is absent.

rule_level_problems.problem: 'No stools or flatus/wind for past 24 hours' is encoded as a conjunction (no stool AND no flatus, both >= 24 h). This is the clinically intended reading (absolute constipation) but a strict 'any of' reading of the red box would use 'or'; worth a one-line note in the rule's description so a reviewer does not flip it.

summary: The red box is encoded completely and correctly: all 15 criteria are in the check_for and the Urgent or-list, the five 'X likely' items are probable rules referenced via active_condition, and the anaphylaxis pre-screen follows the gold-standard pattern. The misses are in the non-urgent flowchart: IBS drops one of the page's four features ('pain relieved with passing stool', a SNOMED gap), GORD applies the 80 cm female waist threshold to everyone because the language has no sex, and the woman-with-lower-abdominal-pain branch (abnormal discharge or pain on moving cervix -> LAP syndrome) has no rule and never checks for 'Pain on movement of cervix' although SNOMED has it. Minor concept questions remain on 'Infectious disease' for 'infection likely' and on 'Blood glucose status' for the glucose vital.
